incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 fired — sierra-tenant: reserved_capacity_throttle (region-us-west)

pd-bot: PagerDuty incident sierra-reserved-capacity-1942005472 created and paging: Maya (oncall). Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD1942005472

Maya (oncall): acked on PagerDuty — taking this. Looking now at dashboards.

Maya (oncall): quick status: 95th latency for sierra-tenant spiking, reserved pool queue growing, errors 429 on generation path. Customer impacted: elevated error rates for their reserved endpoints.

Jordan (SRE): copying metrics — seeing burst from their traffic + many long-lived KV cache misses. Relevant query: `sum(rate(reserved_pool_queue_length{tenant="sierra"}[1m])) by (instance)`

Jordan (SRE): snippet from logs:```
2026-11-05T14:21:17Z ERROR serving request tenant=sierra model=gptx-16q code=429 msg="reserved_pool_throttled" queue_len=124
2026-11-05T14:21:18Z WARN  kvcache miss tenant=sierra key=prefix-abc-123
```

Maya (oncall): thanks. Initial mitigation: increasing reserved pool concurrency for sierra by bumping their pool slot config (temporary). Applying now — will monitor queue drain.

Eli (Platform): heads up — if we bump beyond committed capacity we need to enable burst pool; that will pull on shared capacity. Recommend short window (5m) + fallback model.

Maya (oncall): executed CLI command to increase reserved slots:```
redwood-cli pools update --tenant sierra --reserved-slots 20 --reason "emergency-burst-2026-11-05"
```
Response: `OK pending-provision`

Maya (oncall): queue dropped from 124 -> 32 in ~60s. Error rate down to ~3% from 18%. Latency 95th improving but still noisy.

Priya (CS): pinging Sierra support contact (lena@sierra.co) — letting them know we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA. They reported user-facing errors ~14:20 UTC.

Jordan (SRE): we saw a correlated spike in cache-eviction rate for that tenant's prefix. Likely their workload sent many varied prompts (no prefix reuse) which bypassed KV caching and increased per-token work.

Maya (oncall): enabling fallback policy to lower-capacity, cheaper model to sustain requests if we hit quota again. Command:```
redwood-cli route update --tenant sierra --route /generate --fallback-model gptx-lite --fallback-threshold 0.9
```

Maya (oncall): fallback policy in place. Also added short-term rate-limit to self-serve endpoints for sierra to protect global pool: `limit=300r/m` (applied).

Eli (Platform): allocating burst capacity — note: billing will be flagged for customer manager. Also scheduling ephemeral repro to test KV cache behavior. Jordan, can you grab a flamegraph for the runtime for next 10 minutes?

Jordan (SRE): on it. Starting trace capture: `trace-id=tr_1942005489`. Preliminary flamegraph shows heavy tokenizer GC at 50% CPU time. Might be interplay of many short-lived sessions.

Maya (oncall): timecheck: incident acknowledged at 14:22 — mitigation applied 14:24, errors falling. Escalating to PDL2 because we increased beyond committed cap.

pd-bot: Incident escalated to L2 and emailed infra-ops@redwood.internal.

Eli (Platform): adding a temporary KV cache pin for sierra's hot-prefixes to reduce cache churn. Command:```
platform-tools cache pin --tenant sierra --prefix prefix-abc --duration 30m
```
Result: `pinned 3 keys`

Priya (CS): Sierra says user errors are largely reduced, they see a backlog clearing in their web UI. They appreciate the quick response — asked for timeline and root cause once stable.

Maya (oncall): will keep monitoring until fully stable. If error rate stays below 1% for 10m, we'll close pager but kick off incident follow-up.

Jordan (SRE): putting diagnostic artifacts in the incident channel: dashboards + trace link + repro steps. Repro note: heavy fanout of unique prompt prefixes caused KV miss amplification. Suggest adding advisory to docs about prefix reuse.

Maya (oncall): at 14:33 errors at 0.7%, 95th latency within SLO but still ~20% higher than baseline. Queue ~4.

Alex (oncall-next): I'm taking handoff in ~10m — Maya can you summarize actions for my shift?

Maya (oncall): summary for handoff to Alex: 1) Reserve slots bumped to 20 (temp) 2) Burst pool enabled for 10m window 3) Fallback model gptx-lite enabled for /generate route 4) Pin applied to hot prefix 5) Rate-limit 300r/m applied 6) Trace tr_1942005489 capturing runtime profile 7) CS notified and customer reports improvement

Alex (oncall-next): got it. I'll watch the queue and will leave it in Platform's hands to deprovision after 20m if stable.

Maya (oncall): planning next steps: - revert emergency slot bump once stable - create postmortem ticket and assign Jordan/Eli for RCA - identify config guardrail to prevent accidental huge prefix variance - contact billing/CS for cost of burst

Eli (Platform): agree. Also propose automated detection rule: if reserved_pool_queue_length > 50 for tenant -> auto-fallback and notify CS. Filing a ticket now.

Maya (oncall): closing the pager on PD after 20m stable. PD note: mitigations applied, customer impact reduced, follow-up required.

pd-bot: PagerDuty incident PD1942005472 resolved by Maya (oncall). Resolution: temporary capacity bump + fallback + cache pin. Postmortem requested.

Maya (oncall): adding action items: `#1 run RCA` `#2 alerting rule` `#3 doc update (prefix best practices)` `#4 cost reconciliation`. Assigning to Jordan (RCA) and Eli (automation).

Priya (CS): will coordinate customer comms and gather any logs from Sierra that might help reproduce.

Jordan (SRE): I'll upload flamegraphs and root-cause notes to the incident ticket (INC-1942005472). Expect draft postmortem by EOD tomorrow.

Maya (oncall): thanks team. Handoff to Alex in 5.

Alex (oncall-next): took handoff at 14:53 UTC. Monitoring.

Maya (oncall): signing off. :white_check_mark:

(End thread)
